If you are not directly subject to inappropriate behaviour, but observe it happening to a colleague, you should report your concerns if you feel unable to challenge or tackle this at the time.

If you believe you are experiencing bullying or harassment in the course of your work for NWS, you should refer to the NWS Bullying and Harassment Policy that supports this policy, and which sets out the options available to you.

Employees can seek advice by speaking to their line manager, Trade Union Representative, HR Team, and the anonymous SafeCall helpline 0800 015 5630.

Human Resources Team

The HR Team provide a supportive and guiding role for line managers and employees in the application of the Respect at Work Policy and the procedures and processes that underpin the key principles/commitments.

HR will ensure that line managers and employees are provided with legally complaint, meaningful advice and guidance, in relation to this policy.

Will facilitate meetings between line managers and employees as applicable, to address issues of inappropriate behaviour.

To facilitate and procure the availability of a range of options to resolve an issue ranging from externally facilitate discussions and mediation to formal and independent investigation in a complaint where applicable.

To ensure that all employees are signposted to our people policies as part of their induction into NWS and to monitor and provide regular learning and training on the application of this policy.

To regularly review incidents and outcomes to tackle any problematic areas or trends in the workplace.

Leaders and Managers

It is imperative that the senior leadership team and managers set the tone for NWS and the wider NDA Group.

Demonstrate the NWS Values, encourage and promote an inclusive working environment and to be aware of the impact of their own behaviours on individuals in the workplace environment generally.

Respond positively to any complaints; to challenge and stop unacceptable behaviour in the workplace. Failure to take action to tackle inappropriate behaviour may be considered a failure to fulfil the responsibilities of the position.

Be alert to the possibility that inappropriate behaviour may be happening in their area and to use their judgement to correct behaviour that could be considered offensive; to remind employees and colleagues of the NWS policy on this matter.

Leaders and managers must take prompt action to stop disrespectful and inappropriate behaviour as soon as it is identified and to deal with all incidents quickly, seriously, sensitively, and in confidence, taking advice from HR where appropriate.

Seek advice and support from the HR Team where managers are unsure or unclear of the action to take, and to keep the HR Team up to date on all issues that impact our employees and colleagues.
